questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Extremely difficult. The administration was all over the place, gave unclear guidance and seemed unfamiliar with their own rules. I'll give you two examples.

1) When examining the courses at Panthéon-Sorbonne i needed to find the course catalogues. On their website i could only find the names of the courses for Master students. There was a supposed link to the catalogues but when i clicked the link nothing happened. I made the administration aware of the issue but they did nothing to fix it. Their 'solution' was that they asked me what course descriptions i wanted and then they contacted each professor responsible for the respective courses. It was an extremely inefficient was to organize it which became clear in that it took them 3-4 weeks to gather the descriptions i demanded.

2) On their website exchange students, it was stated very clearly that ERASMUS students on Political Science could only follow 25 ECTS corresponding to 5 courses in the Department of Political Science. As i was obliged by KU to take 30 ECTS/6 courses i asked the administration if this rule was valid. They said yes and told me to take the 6th course in the department of either Law or Economics. 
After searching and searching i found a Law course and ended up registering for that. After my first lecture it was clear that it was extremely difficult and not in any way relevant to me.

Therefore I asked the administration if it was in any way possible for me to take swtich the law course to a Political Science courses despite the aforementioned rule. They replied "of course". As i referred to the rule they had no idea what I was talking about. 

 




2) 25 ECTS

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I followed two courses taught in French and four courses taught in English. The two courses in French were adequately challenging - Not because of the language but the content. The course taught in English were too easy. My guess is that the lower the academic level significantly on courses taught in English as French students' English skills are not too good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Way more old-school teaching, less discussing compared to KU. I missed that.
There was however a lot of presentations which i enjoyed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) The Public, the Private and the Common(s): Neoliberalism and the boundaries of the state.
2) Politics of development in Africa
3) Europe, transnational mobilisations and civil society
4) Administration européenne. 
5) Relations éxterieures de l'UE
6) Visual cultures (.....)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Number 2, 4 and 5.
2) focused on the implications of the involvement of the Western world in Africa. It offered an alternativ perspective the often euro-centric perspectives at KU. 
4) focused on the institutional set-up of the EU on a very detailed manner. I loved that course. 
5) was a role-play focused course where we had to "act" as different European institutions making up a discussing (eg. debate in the Parliament) on the topic for the week.

questions.answer: Ask French people what to do. They have recommendations that you won't find in the guide books.

questions.answer: Mixed. French people are quite confrontative. I had to adapt to that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be mentally prepared for an incompetent administration. You have to ask for the information. 
2) Take as many courses in French as possible.
3) Try and talk to the French students. Some of them are sweet.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See the above

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Culture shocks. The French students in my classes very quite immature and talked during lecture and classes. Very disturbing.
